queries: WITH g AS (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), s AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) * 1.0 AS total, AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT g.SEX, g.cnt AS test_records, g.cnt * 1.0 / s.total AS fraction_of_total, g.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS above_average FROM g CROSS JOIN s WHERE g.cnt > s.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Groups come from an inner join of Laboratory to Patient on ID; a NULL SEX (if any) forms its own group via GROUP BY and is counted among the groups for the average, and the empty string is a separate group.
The per-group average is total matched records divided by the number of groups, and the fraction is the group's count divided by the total matched records.

assumptions.assumption: Groups are the distinct SEX values among laboratory records matched to a patient by an inner join. An empty string is its own group, as the request says. A NULL SEX, if any exists, also forms its own group, because GROUP BY keeps NULLs together and the request does not address it.

The average records per group is the total matched records divided by the number of groups, which is the mean of the group counts. The fraction is the group count divided by the sum of all group counts.

assumptions.assumption: Inner join of Laboratory to Patient on ID drops unmatched lab records. Groups are the distinct SEX values, with the empty string as its own group. Any NULL SEX would also form a group, and it is counted in the average and total.

The 'average number of records per group' is the total number of matched records divided by the number of groups. The fraction is the group count divided by the total of all matched records. The excess is the group count minus the average. Nothing is rounded.
